CheckTitle: Disabled Self-Service Password Reset protects administrator accounts from unauthorized recovery
Description:
The tenant authorization policy property `allowedToUseSSPR` controls whether administrators can reset their own passwords through **Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR)**.

When disabled, password recovery for privileged accounts must go through other administrators or break-glass procedures, reducing the risk of account takeover via compromised recovery methods.
Risk:
If SSPR is enabled for administrators, anyone who controls an admin's registered recovery methods (e.g., **SIM swap**, compromised alternate mailbox, social engineering) can reset the admin password and take over a **privileged account** without going through a controlled recovery process.

This directly threatens the **confidentiality** and **integrity** of the entire tenant.

Code.Other:
Administrator SSPR cannot be disabled from the Microsoft Entra admin center: the **Password reset** settings there only apply to non-administrator users. Use Microsoft Graph PowerShell instead:
1. Connect-MgGraph -Scopes Policy.ReadWrite.Authorization
2. Update-MgPolicyAuthorizationPolicy -AllowedToUseSspr:$false
3. Verify with (Get-MgPolicyAuthorizationPolicy).AllowedToUseSspr

Recommendation.Text:
Disable **Self-Service Password Reset** for administrator accounts. Privileged account password recovery should be handled by other administrators or **break-glass procedures** to prevent account takeover through compromised recovery methods.

Ensure a documented recovery path exists before disabling SSPR for admins.

Notes: The service default for allowedToUseSSPR is true, so most tenants that never changed it will FAIL. Before disabling, ensure there is a documented recovery path for admin passwords (other admins, break-glass accounts). Requires Policy.ReadWrite.Authorization to remediate.
